title: Rookwood Press fewer books essay
brief: I'm Hester Vance, publisher at Rookwood Press, a small independent press with 9 staff, and I want an essay on our site called "Why we print fewer books", for readers who will read it on a laptop at a desk with a coffee. It should read like an essay: headings and paragraphs, with no more than one short list. Sections: "The year we pulped 11000 books": in 2023, returns from shops left us with 11000 unsold copies we had to destroy, and I stood in the warehouse and watched. "What fewer titles buys": we printed 120 titles in 2022 and plan 86 in 2026; the return rate fell from 34 percent to 19 percent, and each book now gets two launch events instead of none. "What we lost": three debut authors we would have taken a chance on, and about a quarter of our backlist in print, and I will not pretend that is nothing. "What we are promising": a short list of three promises, no title without a named champion on staff, no print run above 1.5 times the pre-orders, and a yearly public report on returns, the first due 2027-01-31. End with one pulled-out line: a smaller list is not a smaller ambition. Tone: honest, a little rueful, no marketing language.

visible: a smaller list is not a smaller ambition

edit.request: Change the 2026 plan from 86 titles to 90, the return rate fall to 21 percent instead of 19 percent, and the first report date to 2027-02-28.
